title: Machine learning screens identify ginkgetin, oleandrin and periplocin as senolytics
summary: Machine learning classifiers were trained on 58 known senolytics against a background of 2,523 FDA-approved or late-stage compounds and used to screen chemical libraries. Top candidates were tested in human lung fibroblasts (IMR90) and A549 lung adenocarcinoma cells, yielding three novel senolytics (ginkgetin, oleandrin, periplocin) with potency comparable to current senolytics. Validation is in cell lines only. Preprint of 2022-04-27.
ai_technology: Machine learning classifiers trained on published senolytic data to screen compound libraries
organization: University of Edinburgh (Cancer Research UK Edinburgh Centre; MRC Institute of Genetics and Cancer)

evidence.tested: Experimental validation of top-ranked compounds in IMR90 and A549 cell lines.
evidence.unknown: In vivo activity and safety are not tested in the abstract; full text not reviewed.
